Solan.evidence: CRE, carbapenemase and NDM-1 detected in Solan hospital
MDR E. coli, Pseudomonas and MRSA reported
MDR E. coli and P. aeruginosa detected
Solan included in a multicentre Indian antibiotic-use/knowledge study
Limited publicly available district-level continuous data

Bilaspur.evidence: Limited published isolate-level data. AIIMS Bilaspur monitors resistance, runs an Antimicrobial Stewardship Program and detects AMR genes. Regional Himalayan studies report high carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter and Pseudomonas.
MDR Gram-negative bacteria are expected in hospital settings based on Himachal and national patterns. Specific public reports of MDR E. coli, Pseudomonas or MRSA from Bilaspur hospitals are limited.
The provided evidence reports AIIMS Bilaspur participation in multicentre hospital wastewater AMR surveillance studies linked to ICMR.
No specific published detection of MDR E. coli or P. aeruginosa in Bilaspur municipal wastewater is identified in the provided evidence.
No Bilaspur-specific published study was identified in the provided evidence. Regional lower-Himalayan irrigation water studies report ESBL-positive Gram-negative bacteria.
High empirical antibiotic use and over-the-counter antibiotic sales are reported as statewide concerns in Himachal Pradesh. Bilaspur-specific measurements are not provided.
Limited publicly available continuous district-level AMR data. The provided evidence states that AIIMS Bilaspur is strengthening local monitoring.

Mandi.evidence: Limited published isolate-level data from SLBSGMC Mandi or district hospitals. Regional Himalayan tertiary-care studies report high carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii (68–73%) and Pseudomonas.

MDR patterns are expected in hospital settings based on Himachal statewide data. Specific public reports of MDR E. coli, Klebsiella or MRSA numbers from Mandi hospitals are scarce. MDR-TB is well documented in the district.

No Mandi-specific published detection of MDR organisms in hospital wastewater was identified in the provided evidence. SLBSGMC Mandi and district hospitals generate wastewater, but public testing data are limited.
No specific published MDR E. coli or P. aeruginosa detection from Mandi municipal wastewater was identified in the provided evidence.

No Mandi-specific published studies were identified in the provided evidence. Regional lower-Himalayan irrigation water studies report ESBL-positive Gram-negative bacteria. The provided evidence also mentions colistin-resistant isolates in the Mandi area in a 2021 environmental water study.
High empirical antibiotic use and over-the-counter antibiotic sales are reported as statewide issues in Himachal Pradesh. The provided evidence indicates that Mandi follows the same pattern.
The provided evidence reports strong data availability for MDR-TB. Continuous bacterial AMR surveillance across hospitals and environmental sources remains limited compared with Kangra.

Kangra.evidence: Two-year analysis of urine isolates from DRPGMC Kangra (2024–25) reported high resistance among common uropathogens, including E. coli, Klebsiella and Pseudomonas. Increased resistance to third-generation cephalosporins, fluoroquinolones and carbapenems was reported.
A drug-resistant TB study reported rifampicin resistance in 20% of enrolled patients and 25% of Xpert-positive patients. Reports also mention MDR E. coli, Klebsiella and MRSA from district hospitals.
District-specific hospital wastewater AMR data are limited. Resistant Gram-negative bacteria may be a concern in wastewater from tertiary-care hospitals such as DRPGMC Kangra.
Comprehensive district-level AMR surveillance data for municipal wastewater are not available in the reviewed sources. Urban population growth and tourism indicate a need for monitoring.
Kangra is identified as a comparison site in environmental AMR surveillance research. Regional studies have detected ESBL-producing Gram-negative bacteria in surface and irrigation water.
A community survey in Kangra (2024, n=400) reported that 21.8% purchased antibiotics without a prescription, 19.3% used leftover antibiotics, and 29.8% stopped antibiotics when feeling better.
HISP India has collaborated with DRPGMC Kangra for digital AMR surveillance using a DHIS2-based system. Surveillance exists but is not comprehensive for all bacterial pathogens.

Chamba.evidence: A study at Government Medical College-Chamba (2020) examined 984 patients. Of these, 220 (22.35%) received antibiotics, 52% of prescriptions were reported as irrational, 19.53% involved antibiotic combinations, and fluoroquinolones accounted for 17.36% of prescriptions.

A study of hilly districts in Himachal Pradesh included Chamba in a pooled group with Solan, Shimla and Kullu. The pooled group reported 3 rifampicin-resistant cases among 7 patients. A separate Chamba-specific MDR-TB rate was not available.
No robust Chamba-specific published hospital wastewater AMR surveillance was identified in the reviewed sources. Healthcare facilities generate wastewater that may contribute to environmental AMR.
No Chamba-specific published detection of multidrug-resistant bacteria in municipal wastewater was identified in the reviewed sources.
Strong Chamba-specific published AMR data for irrigation or environmental water were not identified in the reviewed sources.
The Government Medical College-Chamba prescription study (2020) reported substantial antibiotic use and a high proportion of irrational prescribing, indicating antibiotic-use pressure.
General health surveillance exists through systems such as IDSP/IHIP. Comprehensive district-wide bacterial AMR surveillance for Chamba was not publicly documented in the reviewed sources.

Hamirpur.evidence: District-specific routine bacterial AMR surveillance is limited. Published district evidence is stronger for antibiotic use and TB drug resistance than for routine bacterial antibiotic susceptibility testing.

A 2019 study using TB-office data from Hamirpur, Bilaspur and Solan reported pooled MDR-TB prevalence of 3.14% across the three districts. Among new TB cases, prevalence was 2.42%, compared with 9% among previously treated cases. A separate Hamirpur study reported 93 MDR cases among 2,277 TB patients during 2011–2018.

A 2024 Himachal study sampled hospital and pharmaceutical waste-disposal sites, including work based at Career Point University, Hamirpur. Four of 29 isolates were MDR, including Pseudomonas aeruginosa resistant to all 15 tested antibiotics. This is site-level evidence, not district-wide prevalence.
No robust Hamirpur-specific published AMR surveillance dataset for municipal wastewater was identified in the reviewed sources.

No strong Hamirpur-specific published AMR water dataset was identified in the reviewed sources. Broader Himachal environmental studies report ESBL-producing and resistant Gram-negative bacteria in selected watersheds.

District-specific quantitative community antibiotic-consumption data are limited. Irrational prescribing and antimicrobial misuse are recognized AMR drivers, while healthcare connectivity and referral movement may influence antibiotic-use patterns.
General disease and TB surveillance exists, but comprehensive district-wide bacterial AMR surveillance is not publicly documented in the reviewed sources.

Kinnaur.evidence: No routine district-wide bacterial AMR surveillance or antibiogram data for Kinnaur were identified in the reviewed sources. Patients may be referred to higher centres, including IGMC Shimla and regional hospitals, limiting local clinical AMR data.

Drug-resistant TB is a relevant concern in Himachal Pradesh. A high-altitude study reported rifampicin-resistant TB in mountainous districts, but no district-specific MDR-TB estimate for Kinnaur was identified. Kinnaur was selected to launch a TB Elimination Campaign at Sangla in 2022.
No Kinnaur-specific hospital or pharmaceutical waste AMR surveillance data were identified in the reviewed literature. Healthcare facilities generate waste, but site-specific AMR evidence is lacking.

No published detection of multidrug-resistant bacteria in Kinnaur municipal wastewater was identified in the reviewed sources. Monitoring is needed, particularly in growing towns and tourist areas such as Sangla, Kalpa and Reckong Peo.

A 2023 study in lower Himalayan agro-ecosystems reported multidrug-resistant and ESBL-producing Gram-negative bacteria in irrigation-purpose wastewater. District-specific results for Kinnaur were not provided.

A 2024 study surveyed 162 farmers from high-altitude Lahaul, Spiti and Kinnaur and reported antibiotic-use practices involving yaks, dzomo and hill cattle. The findings indicate veterinary antibiotic use in the high-altitude livestock context, but do not establish a Kinnaur-specific prevalence rate.

General disease surveillance exists through systems such as IDSP/IHIP and the National TB Elimination Programme. Comprehensive district-wide bacterial AMR surveillance covering clinical, environmental and One Health settings is not publicly documented in the reviewed sources.

Kullu.evidence: No comprehensive Kullu-specific bacterial AMR surveillance or antibiogram data found in reviewed literature. Patients are often referred to higher centres such as IGMC Shimla and DRPGMC Kangra, limiting local clinical AMR data.

Kullu was included in the 'Others' category in a multi-district study on rifampicin-resistant TB in Himachal Pradesh. A separate district-specific MDR-TB rate was not reported. TB remains a concern in hilly regions due to difficult terrain and delayed diagnosis.
No Kullu-specific hospital or pharmaceutical waste AMR surveillance was found. Healthcare facilities generate biomedical waste, but site-specific AMR data are lacking.
No published detection of MDR bacteria in Kullu municipal wastewater was found in reviewed sources. Tourism and urbanisation around Manali and surrounding areas may increase potential AMR spread.

ICAR-DCFR reported antimicrobial resistance in E. coli isolates from fish farms in Kullu-Mandi and Bilaspur districts, including resistance to ampicillin (29.4%), cefoxitin (27.5%) and cefotaxime (23.5%).

Quantitative district-specific community antibiotic-consumption data are unavailable. Irrational antibiotic use, self-medication and incomplete courses may contribute to AMR. Tourism and seasonal population influx in Manali may increase antibiotic use.
General disease surveillance exists through IDSP/IHIP. Comprehensive district-wide bacterial AMR surveillance covering clinical, environmental and One Health settings is not publicly documented.

Lahaul and Spiti.evidence: No Lahaul and Spiti-specific bacterial AMR surveillance or antibiogram data were identified in reviewed literature. Patients are commonly referred to higher centres, including IGMC Shimla, Tanda, Manali and DRPGMC Kangra, limiting local clinical AMR data. Imported AMR risk cannot be excluded.

Lahaul and Spiti was included in the 'Others' category in a multi-district Himachal study on rifampicin-resistant TB. No separate district-specific MDR-TB rate was available. Remote, high-altitude terrain can delay diagnosis and access to diagnostic facilities.

No Lahaul and Spiti-specific hospital or pharmaceutical-waste AMR data were identified. Healthcare facilities, including the district hospital at Keylong and smaller CHCs, generate biomedical waste, but site-specific AMR data are lacking.

No published detection of MDR bacteria in Lahaul and Spiti municipal wastewater was found in reviewed literature. Sewage infrastructure is limited and the population is small, although tourism inflows around Keylong and Jispa may increase future monitoring needs.

No Lahaul & Spiti-specific AMR data for irrigation or environmental water were identified. Studies from lower-Himalayan districts such as Solan, Sirmaur and Kangra have reported ESBL-producing and multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria in water sources; these are regional findings, not district-specific detections.

No quantitative district-specific antibiotic-consumption data are available. In remote high-altitude areas, empirical antibiotic use may be influenced by limited diagnostic facilities and difficult healthcare access. Seasonal tourism and livestock, including yaks, dzomo, sheep and goats, may also affect antibiotic-use pressure.

General disease surveillance exists through district IDSP/IHIP reporting units. Dedicated comprehensive bacterial AMR surveillance across clinical, environmental and One Health settings is not publicly documented for Lahaul & Spiti.

Shimla.evidence: IGMC Shimla is identified as the only NARS-Net AMR surveillance laboratory in Himachal Pradesh. Clinical studies from IGMC report multidrug-resistant organisms, including MRSA, ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae, and carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter and Pseudomonas in clinical samples. Patients referred from across the state increase the importance of responsible antibiotic use and surveillance.

Rifampicin-resistant TB has been reported in Himachal Pradesh, with Shimla included in multi-district hilly-region studies. Shimla contributes cases to the state TB programme, although an exact separate district-specific rate was not reported in the cited summary.

Shimla has a high concentration of healthcare facilities, including IGMC, private hospitals and diagnostic centres, generating biomedical and pharmaceutical waste. Himachal environmental studies have recovered multidrug-resistant bacteria, including Pseudomonas species, from hospital/pharmaceutical waste sites, including Shimla.

A 2026 study reported a multidrug-resistant Enterobacter bugandensis isolate from Shimla wastewater carrying multiple antimicrobial-resistance genes, including beta-lactamases. This indicates clinically relevant resistant bacteria in urban wastewater.

Strong Shimla-specific published AMR data for irrigation water were not identified in the provided summary. Studies in other Himachal districts, including Solan, Sirmaur and Kangra, report ESBL-producing and multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria in water sources, indicating a regional concern rather than confirmed Shimla-specific prevalence.

As a major tertiary-care and referral centre, IGMC Shimla has substantial antibiotic use. Empirical prescribing, self-medication and inappropriate use are recognised AMR drivers. High tourist influx during peak seasons may also increase community antibiotic use.

IGMC Shimla is a NARS-Net site and provides regular WHONET-based AMR surveillance data. Comprehensive district-wide surveillance across community, environmental and One Health settings remains limited beyond the medical-college network.

Sirmaur.evidence: No comprehensive Sirmaur-specific bacterial AMR surveillance or antibiogram data were available in the reviewed literature. Patients with severe infections may be referred to higher centres such as IGMC Shimla. Regional Himachal studies report multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria in clinical settings, but these do not establish Sirmaur-specific prevalence.

Sirmaur was not separately reported in major district-wise MDR-TB studies and was included in an 'Others' category in one study. Rifampicin-resistant TB has been reported in Himachal Pradesh's hilly districts, making it a regional concern, but a Sirmaur-specific rate was not available.

No Sirmaur-specific hospital or pharmaceutical-waste AMR data were identified. Healthcare facilities generate biomedical waste that may contribute to environmental AMR, but site-specific evidence is lacking.

Sirmaur-specific municipal wastewater AMR surveillance is limited. Urbanisation in areas such as Paonta Sahib and Nahan may increase the importance of wastewater monitoring, but published district-specific data are limited.

A 2023 study analysed irrigation-purpose wastewater from 10 Sirmaur locations, including Baru Sahib, Kakli, Lana Machher, Kheri, Dadahu and Rajgarh. It detected resistant Gram-negative bacteria including E. coli, Enterobacter, Hafnia, Shigella, Citrobacter and Klebsiella, with ESBL-producing isolates indicating environmental AMR.

District-specific quantitative community antibiotic-consumption data are not available. Irrational antibiotic use, self-medication and incomplete courses are recognised regional drivers. Agricultural activities, horticulture and livestock may also contribute to environmental antibiotic-use pressure.

General disease surveillance exists through IDSP/IHIP reporting units. Comprehensive district-wide bacterial AMR surveillance across clinical, environmental and One Health settings is not publicly documented for Sirmaur.

Una.evidence: No comprehensive Una-specific bacterial AMR or antibiogram dataset was identified in the reviewed public literature. Regional Hospital Una and district health facilities provide clinical services, but routine district-wide bacterial resistance data are not publicly documented.

A study of DR-TB suspects referred from Kangra and Una (July 2012–June 2013) included 89 smear-positive patients and 79 Xpert-positive patients. Rifampicin resistance was 11/89 (12.4%) among smear-positive patients and 11/79 (14%) among Xpert-positive patients. These are results among evaluated patients, not population prevalence estimates.

No Una-specific published AMR surveillance dataset for hospital or pharmaceutical waste was identified. District healthcare facilities generate biomedical waste, but resistant-organism surveillance is a data gap.

No robust Una-specific published dataset detecting multidrug-resistant bacteria or AMR in municipal wastewater was identified in the reviewed sources. Urban growth and healthcare wastewater support the need for targeted monitoring.

No strong Una-specific published AMR dataset for irrigation water was identified. Environmental studies in other Himachal districts, including Solan, Sirmaur and Kangra, report ESBL-producing and multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria in irrigation-purpose wastewater. These regional findings support surveillance rather than assuming Una is low risk.

District-specific quantitative antibiotic-consumption data are limited. Empirical prescribing, self-medication and incomplete antibiotic courses are recognised AMR drivers; local pharmacy and prescription audits would be needed to measure these practices in Una.

Una has district TB services and routine public-health reporting, but comprehensive clinical, environmental and One Health AMR surveillance is not publicly documented. A district TB centre is listed under the state TB programme.
